Chill guy
CHIL gy
noun phrase (Gen-Z slang)
From a drawing by the artist Phillip Banks, posted in October 2023, of a cartoon dog in a grey sweater, rolled-up jeans, and red sneakers, hands in pockets, with a faint smirk. In November 2024 it exploded on TikTok and X as the "chill guy" meme, in videos captioned with variations of "just a chill guy who lowkey doesn’t care" (the original caption used a crude acronym) set over stressful situations the chill guy shrugs off. Chill for relaxed is older American slang: chill out (c. 1979, spread by 1980s hip-hop), and the adjective chill, easygoing, in the 1990s.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In current slang the chill guy is the meme of easy composure: a cartoon dog with his hands in his pockets, unbothered while the exam is failing, the car is towed, or the group project collapses. Teens post themselves as the chill guy to laugh at their own stress, and "he’s a chill guy" is high praise among boys. The Christian observation: there is a composure Scripture loves and one it rebukes, and the meme mixes them. The good one is real: "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God" (Php 4:6), and "the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus" (Php 4:7). "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee" (Isa 26:3). The calmest man in the Gospels is the Lord Jesus "in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow" while His disciples panicked (Mar 4:38) — and when He woke He did not shrug; He rebuked the wind. His calm came from trusting His Father, not from not caring. The bad composure is the sluggard’s: "Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep" (Pro 6:10). Hands in pockets while the work goes undone is not peace; it is the road to want. A father tells his son: be calm in a crisis and never careless about your duty. Pray, then work. The calm that comes from trusting God takes the hands out of the pockets.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen-Z meme (Phillip Banks drawing, 2023; viral November 2024) of easy, hands-in-pockets composure — a calm Scripture commends when it rests on trusting God and rebukes when it is the sluggard’s shrug.

CHILL GUY, n. phr. (Gen-Z slang, 2024–present; internet meme) One who stays relaxed and unbothered under pressure; from the "just a chill guy" cartoon dog. "Phone at two percent, no charger, I’m a chill guy."

Used of oneself in self-mockery during stress, and of others as praise: "He’s a chill guy," easygoing, low-drama. The image itself is posted as a reaction.

Older slang: chill, chill out (1980s–90s), relax; a chill person, easy company. Before that, chill meant cold, and a chill the shiver before a fever.

Webster (1828), root word chill: “CHILL, noun 1. A shivering with cold; rigors, as in an ague; the cold fit that precedes a fever; sensation of cold in an animal body; chilliness. [&hellip;] 2. A moderate degree of cold; chilliness in any body; that which gives the sensation of cold.”

Decode for parents: when your son says he is a chill guy about the test, he may be joking about his nerves or announcing that he has stopped studying; ask which.

Key Scripture

Php 4:6 — "Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God."

Php 4:7 — "And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus."

Isa 26:3 — "Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee."

Mar 4:38 — "And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?"

Pro 6:10 — "Yet a little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to sleep:"

Modern Corruption

The chill guy meme blurs the peace of a man who trusts God with the shrug of a man who has stopped caring, and the hands in its pockets belong to the second.

expand to see more

Much of the meme is harmless self-mockery — a stressed teenager laughing at himself — and there is a real virtue near it. Scripture forbids fretting: "Be careful for nothing" (Php 4:6). It promises peace to the mind stayed on God (Isa 26:3). A boy who can keep his head when the bus breaks down is learning something good, and "He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty" (Pro 16:32).

But the chill guy’s calm has no source. He is unbothered because he has decided not to be bothered, and his hands stay in his pockets. That is the posture Proverbs warns against: "a little folding of the hands to sleep" ends in want that comes "as an armed man" (Pro 6:10–11). Christ’s calm in the storm was the calm of a Son resting in His Father, and it rose up to act. Teach your children the difference: peace that prays and then works, not indifference that shrugs and then drifts.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English ciele (cold) → chill, coldness → c. 1980 chill out, relax → 2023 drawing, 2024 meme: just a chill guy.
